messages:
sophia: Quick idea — we should formalize a routing matrix that picks model variant by (customer_tier, region) and defines explicit fallback order + quota behavior. Posting a minimal sketch for discussion.

kevin: paste the sketch pls. Are you thinking per-request overrides or account-level defaults?

sophia: per-account defaults + optional per-route override. Minimal sketch below (YAML-ish):
```
routing:
  default:
    free:
      variant: small-v1
      fallbacks: [small-v2, medium-quant]
  pro:
    us-east:
      variant: medium-v2
      fallbacks: [medium-quant, small-v2]
    eu-west:
      variant: medium-eu
      fallbacks: [small-eu, medium-quant-eu]
  enterprise:
    variant: large-v1
    fallbacks: [large-quant, medium-v2]
quota:
  hard_limits:
    free: 100000_tokens/day
    pro: 2000000_tokens/day
    enterprise: 100000000_tokens/day
  soft_degrade: true
```

maria: a couple concerns: billing/usage attribution when fallback fires; also observability — need clear telemetry that indicates which variant served a token + which fallback triggered.

raj: also latency cliff when we fall back across regions or to quantized models. Need SLOs per-variant and a cheap fallback path that preserves latency for interactive apps.

kevin: agree. For quotas: do we want hard-enforced quotas (reject) or soft-degrade where we route to cheaper variant and keep serving? My vote: soft by default for free/pro, hard for enterprise only if explicit.

sophia: that's my leaning too. soft_degrade: true in sketch. But we need an API-level flag to allow customers to opt into "strict_quota_enforcement": true for compliance-sensitive flows.

devex-bot: note — if we add per-route overrides we'll need SDK changes: include `routing_hint` and `strict_quota` params in the request shape. Also update quickstarts.

maria: telemetry plan: emit metric labels {requested_variant, served_variant, fallback_reason, tier, region}. That lets us compute fallback rates and cost delta. Also log per-account quota windows.

raj: perf test plan: create synthetic workload that triggers 10% intentional overload and measure p95 latency and fallback-rate per-tier/region/variant. I'll run it in staging cluster.

kevin: what about console UX? We need a matrix editor that shows default for each tier+region and an override UI for routes. Also a diff/preview when you change it so you can see estimated cost impact.

sophia: +1. rough rollout: 1) infra + runtime hooks to apply routing policies and emit labels, 2) SDK add `routing_hint` + `strict_quota`, 3) console matrix editor + cost preview, 4) gradual rollout to free/pro with soft_degrade enabled, enterprise opt-in for hard limits.

infra-bot: recent staging run: fallback-rate=0.4% for medium-v2->medium-quant under 2x load, p95 increase=12ms. (just FYI)

kevin: nice. action items: sophia open RFC with config schema + API changes; maria own metrics schema + dashboard; raj run perf tests and capture latency cliff cases; devex to mock SDK changes; infra to add runtime labels + budget enforcement hooks.

sophia: sounds good — I'll open the RFC this afternoon. tagging @maria @raj @kevin for followups. :thumbsup:

maria: adding a note — for billing we should store both requested_variant and served_variant in usage events so we can compute refunds or promos if fallback was to a cheaper model.

raj: one more: edge case when region variant is unavailable but another region has capacity — do we cross-region fallback? my thought: prefer same-region quantized fallback first, then same-tier cross-region only if latency budget allows. Need policy param for `cross_region_fallback: allow|disallow|latency_threshold_ms`.

kevin: yes add that to schema. ok wrapping up — RFC incoming.

sophia: thanks everyone. I'll include a small example policy generator so infra can load staged configs.

infra-bot: ack — will watch the RFC and prepare a PR template for config tests.
